source: Written by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from the county counts (AP via The New York Times), the 2024 baseline and Census ACS 2023 context.

45067.t: Marion County backed Democrat Annie Andrews over Republican Darline Graham in the U.S. Senate race by 27 points, 7,085 votes to 4,036, with 99% of the expected vote counted. Kamala Harris had carried it by 11 points in 2024, so the county moved 17 points toward the Democrats. That is a smaller shift than in most of South Carolina, where every county moved left and the typical one moved 21 points; Marion ranks 39th of 46. Similar counties moved by comparable amounts: Fairfield 15, Hampton 12, Bamberg 17. About 11,263 votes were cast, 84% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

45001.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Abbeville County backed Republican Darline Graham over Democrat Annie Andrews by 22 points, 5,364 votes to 3,415. That is 21 points closer than Trump's 42-point win here in 2024, almost exactly the typical South Carolina county's shift of 21 points, as Andrews carried the state by 5 after Trump won it by 18. All 46 counties in the state moved toward the Democrats. Similar nearby counties moved by comparable amounts: Saluda by 21 points, Union by 21 and Laurens by 25.

Abbeville cast 9,026 votes, 75% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot tell how much of the shift came from voters changing their minds and how much from who stayed home.

45047.t:
Greenwood County stayed Republican in the U.S. Senate race but by far less. Darline Graham beat Annie Andrews 12,629 to 11,352, a margin of 5 points, down from Donald Trump's 29-point win here in 2024. That 24-point swing toward the Democrats is slightly larger than the state's 22-point move and the typical South Carolina county's 21, ranking 9th of 46. Similar counties moved by comparable amounts: Kershaw by 27 points to a 1-point Republican edge, Chesterfield by 23 and Edgefield by 19.

Turnout was 24,618 votes, 80% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell how much of the shift came from voters changing their minds and how much from who stayed home.

45065.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Annie Andrews (D) and Darline Graham (R), McCormick County moved about 11 points toward the Democrats, from a 17-point Trump win in 2024 to a 6-point Graham win, 2,829 votes to 2,518. That is the smallest shift of South Carolina's 46 counties, all of which moved left. The typical county there moved 21 points, and the state swung 22 as Andrews won by about 5. Comparable counties went further: Barnwell moved 19 points, Calhoun 21 and Chester 23, and all three flipped to Andrews.

Turnout was 5,470 votes, 89% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

45085.t:

That 22-point shift toward the Democrats matches the statewide move and sits slightly above the typical South Carolina county's 21. Sumter ranks 19th of 46 counties by size of move, and every county in the state moved left. Among counties with similar 2024 results, Charleston and Marlboro moved about as much, 20 and 21 points, while Hampton moved 12.

Turnout was 36,466 votes, 81% of the 2024 total. Because of that drop, the count cannot tell how much of the shift came from voters changing their minds and how much from voters who stayed home.

That 23-point move toward the Democrats closely matched the state's 22-point shift and ranks 15th among South Carolina's 46 counties, every one of which moved left. The typical county in the state moved 21 points; nationally, the typical move was 14.

Turnout was 17,648 votes, 71% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Similar counties moved by about as much: Oconee 20 points, Pickens 23 and Anderson 24.
